title: Luke Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 8.

questions.question: In Luke 8, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus went throughout every city and village preaching
Mary called Magdalene was healed of seven devils
Jesus spoke a parable of the sower
The disciples asked Jesus about the parable
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus went throughout every city and village preaching
questions.explanation: This event is described first in Luke 8:1, before the mention of Mary Magdalene (v.2), the parable (v.4), or the disciples' question (v.9).

questions.question: Who was healed of seven devils according to Luke 8?
questions.correctAnswer: Mary called Magdalene
questions.explanation: Luke 8:2 states that Mary called Magdalene had seven devils cast out of her.

questions.question: Who was Joanna in Luke 8?
options: The wife of Chuza, Herod's steward
The mother of John the Baptist
questions.correctAnswer: The wife of Chuza, Herod's steward
questions.explanation: Luke 8:3 identifies Joanna as the wife of Chuza, who was Herod's steward.

questions.question: According to Luke 8, what did many women do for Jesus?
options: Ministered unto him of their substance
Preached with him in cities and villages
questions.correctAnswer: Ministered unto him of their substance
questions.explanation: Luke 8:3 says many women ministered to Jesus of their substance.

questions.question: In Luke 8, what did the sower do with the seed?
options: Sowed it, some fell by the wayside
questions.correctAnswer: Sowed it, some fell by the wayside
questions.explanation: Luke 8:5 describes the sower sowing seed, some falling by the wayside.

questions.question: What happened to the seed that fell upon the rock in Luke 8?
options: It withered away because it lacked moisture
questions.correctAnswer: It withered away because it lacked moisture
questions.explanation: Luke 8:6 states the seed on the rock withered away because it lacked moisture.

questions.question: According to Luke 8, what choked the seed that fell among thorns?
options: The thorns sprang up and choked it
questions.correctAnswer: The thorns sprang up and choked it
questions.explanation: Luke 8:7 explains that the thorns sprang up with the seed and choked it.

questions.question: What fruit did the seed on good ground produce according to Luke 8?
questions.correctAnswer: An hundredfold
questions.explanation: Luke 8:8 states the seed on good ground sprang up and bore fruit an hundredfold.

questions.question: Who asked Jesus about the meaning of the parable in Luke 8?
questions.correctAnswer: His disciples
questions.explanation: Luke 8:9 says Jesus’s disciples asked him about the parable’s meaning.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the mysteries of the kingdom of God in Luke 8?
options: It is given to the disciples to know
It is known to all equally
It is hidden from the disciples
It is only revealed after death
questions.correctAnswer: It is given to the disciples to know
questions.explanation: Luke 8:10 says it is given to the disciples to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God.

questions.question: In Luke 8, what is the seed in the parable said to represent?
questions.correctAnswer: The word of God
questions.explanation: Luke 8:11 explains the seed is the word of God.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said no one puts a candle under a bed but sets it on a candlestick.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 8:16 states no man puts a candle under a bed but sets it on a candlestick.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said that nothing secret will remain hidden but will be made manifest.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 8:17 affirms that nothing secret shall remain hidden but will be known and come abroad.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 8 says Jesus was born in Bethlehem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 8 does not mention Jesus’ birth or Bethlehem; this is not stated in the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 8, Jesus healed a blind man in this chapter.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 8 does not describe Jesus healing a blind man; this event is not recorded in these verses.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about his mother and brethren when told they were desiring to see him?
options: My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it.
They are outside waiting for me.
questions.correctAnswer: My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it.
questions.explanation: This is the answer found in Luke 8:21, where Jesus defines his true family as those who hear and obey God's word.

questions.question: What does Luke 8:21 promise will happen if someone hears the word of God and does it?
options: They will be part of Jesus' family.
questions.correctAnswer: They will be part of Jesus' family.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:21 indicates that those who hear and do God's word are considered Jesus' true family, thus promising inclusion in His spiritual family.

questions.question: What did Jesus instruct his disciples to do on a certain day?
options: Let us go over unto the other side of the lake.
questions.correctAnswer: Let us go over unto the other side of the lake.
questions.explanation: This instruction is found in Luke 8:22, where Jesus directs His disciples to launch forth across the lake.

questions.question: What happened while Jesus and his disciples were sailing?
options: They encountered a storm of wind on the lake.
questions.correctAnswer: They encountered a storm of wind on the lake.
questions.explanation: According to Luke 8:23, a storm arose while they were sailing, which put them in jeopardy.

questions.question: What did the disciples say to Jesus when they woke him during the storm?
questions.correctAnswer: Master, master, we perish.
questions.explanation: This is found in Luke 8:24, where the disciples express their fear of drowning to Jesus as they wake Him.

questions.question: What question did Jesus ask his disciples after calming the storm?
options: What do you want from me?
questions.correctAnswer: Where is your faith?
questions.explanation: In Luke 8:25, Jesus questions the disciples about their faith after He calms the storm, indicating the importance of trust in Him.

questions.question: What did the man possessed by devils wear?
questions.correctAnswer: No clothes.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:27 describes the man as having no clothes, highlighting his state of affliction and separation from society.

questions.question: What did the demons call themselves when Jesus asked for their name?
questions.correctAnswer: Legion.
questions.explanation: This is stated in Luke 8:30, where the man possessed by many devils identifies them as 'Legion' due to their number.

questions.question: What did the devils request Jesus not to do?
options: Do not send us to hell.
questions.correctAnswer: Do not torment me.
questions.explanation: The request of the demons is found in Luke 8:28, where they plead with Jesus not to torment them.

questions.question: What did the herd of swine do after the devils entered them?
options: Ran violently down a steep place into the lake.
questions.correctAnswer: Ran violently down a steep place into the lake.
questions.explanation: This is described in Luke 8:33, where the herd of swine, possessed by the devils, ran into the lake and drowned.

questions.question: What was the reaction of those who fed the swine after seeing what happened?
options: They fled and told it in the city.
They tried to capture the devils.
questions.correctAnswer: They fled and told it in the city.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:34 states that those who fed the swine fled to report what had occurred after witnessing the event.

questions.question: What was the state of the man after the demons left him?
options: Sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed, and in his right mind.
questions.correctAnswer: Sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed, and in his right mind.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:35 describes the man after his healing, emphasizing his restored state and peace in Jesus' presence.

questions.question: Did the whole multitude of the Gadarenes ask Jesus to stay with them after the miracle?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to Luke 8:37, the multitude besought Jesus to depart from them out of fear, not to stay.

questions.question: Jesus allowed the man who was healed to stay with him after the healing.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In Luke 8:38, Jesus sent the healed man away, indicating he had a mission to fulfill rather than staying with Jesus.

questions.question: The disciples showed great faith during the storm and did not fear.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 8:25 reveals that the disciples were afraid, questioning Jesus about their peril, indicating a lack of faith during the storm.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 8.

questions.question: After Jesus healed the man possessed by many devils, what did Jesus instruct him to do?
options: Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee.
Follow me and preach to the cities.
Go to the priests for cleansing.
Stay close to Jesus at all times.
questions.correctAnswer: Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:39 states Jesus said, 'Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee.'

questions.question: How did the people react when Jesus returned to the city after healing the demon-possessed man?
options: The people gladly received him: for they were all waiting for him.
They ignored him and went about their business.
questions.correctAnswer: The people gladly received him: for they were all waiting for him.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:40 says, 'the people gladly received him: for they were all waiting for him.'

questions.question: Who came to Jesus pleading for the healing of his dying daughter?
options: A man named Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue.
questions.correctAnswer: A man named Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:41 identifies the man as 'Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue.'

questions.question: For how many years had the woman with the issue of blood suffered and sought healing before touching Jesus’ garment?
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve years
questions.explanation: Luke 8:43 states, 'a woman having an issue of blood twelve years.'

questions.question: What did Jesus perceive had happened when the woman touched the border of His garment?
options: Virtue is gone out of me.
Power has been restored to me.
Faith has increased in the crowd.
questions.correctAnswer: Virtue is gone out of me.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:46 says, 'Somebody hath touched me: for I perceive that virtue is gone out of me.'

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the woman after she confessed her healing by touching His garment?
options: Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.
Rise and walk in the name of the Lord.
Your sins are forgiven; be healed.
questions.correctAnswer: Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:48 records Jesus saying, 'Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'virtue' (dunamis) in Luke 8:46 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Power or miraculous ability
questions.explanation: 'Dunamis' in Greek signifies 'power' or 'miraculous ability,' as used in Luke 8:46 referring to the power going out of Jesus.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in the account of Jairus’s daughter’s death and resurrection in Luke 8:49-56?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Luke 8:49-56 uses a chiasm structure: death (49-50), Jesus’ authority and faith (50-52), rejection (53), and resurrection (54-56).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of Jesus raising Jairus’s daughter as found in Luke 8:54-55?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:17-24 recounts Elijah raising the widow’s son, echoing the resurrection theme in Luke 8:54-55.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the parable of the sower in Luke 8:4-15 by explaining the meaning of the seed as the word of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Mark 4:1-20
questions.explanation: Mark 4:1-20 parallels Luke 8:4-15, explaining the parable of the sower and the seed as the word of God.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the healing of the demon-possessed man in Luke 8:27-39?
options: Jesus calming the storm on the lake.
Jesus preaching the parable of the sower.
Jesus being questioned by the Pharisees.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus calming the storm on the lake.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:23-25 describes Jesus calming the storm, which immediately precedes the healing narrative starting at verse 26.

questions.question: What theological theme is highlighted by Jesus allowing only Peter, James, and John, along with the girl's parents, to enter the room where Jairus’s daughter was?
options: The special role of the inner circle of disciples and faith.
The exclusivity of salvation to the chosen few.
The rejection of family in favor of spiritual kinship.
The public demonstration of miracles before crowds.
questions.correctAnswer: The special role of the inner circle of disciples and faith.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:51 shows Jesus permitting only Peter, James, John, and the parents to witness, emphasizing the privileged role of the closest followers in faith events.

questions.question: How does Luke 8:52-53 demonstrate the cultural context of death and mourning in first-century Judaism?
options: People wept and bewailed, expressing grief openly, but mocked Jesus’ claim that she was only sleeping.
Mourning was a private affair, and people avoided public displays of grief.
The dead were immediately buried without any lamentation.
People believed in reincarnation and thus had little fear of death.
questions.correctAnswer: People wept and bewailed, expressing grief openly, but mocked Jesus’ claim that she was only sleeping.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:52-53 highlights open mourning but also skepticism, reflecting Jewish customs and beliefs about death at that time.

questions.question: What typological significance does the healing of the woman with the issue of blood have in the context of Levitical purity laws?
options: It symbolizes restoration and cleansing beyond ceremonial law, showing Jesus' authority over impurity.
It reinforces strict adherence to Old Testament purity laws.
It depicts the futility of faith without works.
It indicates the rejection of women in religious healing.
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes restoration and cleansing beyond ceremonial law, showing Jesus' authority over impurity.
questions.explanation: The woman’s healing in Luke 8:43-48 illustrates Jesus transcending Levitical impurity, signifying spiritual restoration.

questions.question: What foreshadowing is present in Jesus’ statement 'she is not dead, but sleepeth' in Luke 8:52?
options: It foreshadows Jesus’ own death and resurrection.
It predicts the destruction of the Temple.
It hints at the coming of the Holy Spirit.
It anticipates the fall of Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Jesus’ own death and resurrection.
questions.explanation: Luke 8:52 uses 'sleep' as a metaphor for death, a common New Testament foreshadowing of resurrection including Jesus’ own.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 8:11 teach about salvation?
options: The Word of God is the seed that brings spiritual life
Salvation is based on works and merit
Faith alone is insufficient for salvation
Salvation is only for the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: The Word of God is the seed that brings spiritual life
questions.explanation: Luke 8:11 explicitly states that 'The seed is the word of God,' indicating that salvation comes through hearing and receiving God's word.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 8:15 teach about sanctification?
options: Sanctification requires an honest and good heart that keeps the word and produces fruit with patience
Sanctification is instantaneous and without growth
Sanctification is guaranteed regardless of heart condition
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification requires an honest and good heart that keeps the word and produces fruit with patience
questions.explanation: Luke 8:15 describes the good ground as those who have an honest and good heart, keep the word, and bring forth fruit with patience, teaching the progressive nature of sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 8:10 teach concerning divine revelation and human understanding?
options: The mysteries of the kingdom are revealed to the disciples but hidden from others through parables
Everyone has equal access to understanding the kingdom without mystery
Parables are meant to clarify the kingdom to all equally
The kingdom is fully revealed to the crowds publicly
questions.correctAnswer: The mysteries of the kingdom are revealed to the disciples but hidden from others through parables
questions.explanation: Luke 8:10 states that the disciples are given the knowledge of the kingdom's mysteries, but others hear in parables so they might not understand, emphasizing selective divine revelation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 8:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: In Luke 8:24, Jesus rebukes the wind and raging water, showing His sovereign control over creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 8:46 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Jesus perceives that virtue (power) has gone out of Him when the woman touches Him (Luke 8:46), demonstrating His omniscience in knowing what has happened despite the crowd.

questions.question: How does Luke 8:22–25 prepare for the theme of Jesus’ authority over nature in the New Testament?
options: It demonstrates Jesus’ divine authority, prefiguring His ultimate lordship over all creation
It shows Jesus’ dependence on natural forces
It denies Jesus’ power over nature
It emphasizes human control over the environment
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates Jesus’ divine authority, prefiguring His ultimate lordship over all creation
questions.explanation: Luke 8:22–25 shows Jesus calming the storm, illustrating His divine authority over nature, a theme developed throughout the New Testament as a proof of His deity.

questions.question: How does the healing of the demon-possessed man in Luke 8:26–39 connect to Old Testament themes of deliverance?
options: It fulfills the theme of God's power to liberate His people from bondage
It contradicts Old Testament teachings about spirits
It isolates Jesus from the people
It emphasizes human effort over divine action
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the theme of God's power to liberate His people from bondage
questions.explanation: The deliverance of the man possessed by many demons reflects Old Testament motifs of God freeing His people from spiritual and physical captivity (e.g., Exodus), highlighting Jesus as the divine liberator.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 11 and 15 teach about the Word of God and the believer’s response?
options: The Word of God is the seed that requires a good and honest heart to produce fruit
The Word of God automatically produces fruit regardless of the heart
The Word of God is irrelevant to sanctification
The Word of God is only symbolic, not effective
questions.correctAnswer: The Word of God is the seed that requires a good and honest heart to produce fruit
questions.explanation: Luke 8:11 explains the seed is the Word of God, and Luke 8:15 teaches that the good ground (honest and good heart) is necessary to keep the word and bring forth fruit, combining to show the necessity of faith and perseverance.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 12 and 14 teach about spiritual opposition and worldly distractions?
options: Satan and worldly cares work to prevent belief and fruitfulness
Spiritual opposition is insignificant compared to faith
Worldly riches always lead to sanctification
The devil has no influence on the believer’s heart
questions.correctAnswer: Satan and worldly cares work to prevent belief and fruitfulness
questions.explanation: Luke 8:12 shows the devil takes away the word from the heart, and Luke 8:14 shows worldly cares choke the word, teaching that both spiritual opposition and earthly distractions hinder salvation and sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 18 and 21 teach about the importance of hearing and doing the word of God?
options: Hearing and doing the word identifies true kinship with Christ and results in spiritual increase
Hearing alone is sufficient for salvation
Family ties are more important than spiritual obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Hearing and doing the word identifies true kinship with Christ and results in spiritual increase
questions.explanation: Luke 8:18 warns to take heed how one hears for increase, and Luke 8:21 defines Jesus’ true family as those who hear and do God’s word, linking obedience to spiritual identity and growth.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jesus’ command over the storm in Luke 8:22–25 is a myth. What does the passage actually teach?
options: Jesus displays authoritative power over nature, calming the storm by divine command
Jesus relies on natural forces to calm the storm
The storm is an allegory unrelated to Jesus’ power
The disciples saved themselves without Jesus’ help
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus displays authoritative power over nature, calming the storm by divine command
questions.explanation: Luke 8:24 shows Jesus rebuking the wind and water, which immediately ceased, demonstrating His divine authority rather than myth or human effort.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 8:8 teach about the necessity of spiritual perception in understanding God's kingdom?
options: Spiritual hearing and understanding are necessary to grasp the kingdom's truths
All hearers automatically understand the kingdom
The kingdom is only for the wise of this world
The kingdom's message is purely symbolic
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual hearing and understanding are necessary to grasp the kingdom's truths
questions.explanation: Luke 8:8 ends with 'He that hath ears to hear, let him hear,' emphasizing the necessity of spiritual discernment to understand the kingdom.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Jesus’ healing of the woman with the issue of blood in Luke 8:47–48?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: In Luke 8:48, Jesus comforts the woman, affirming her faith made her whole, demonstrating His mercy towards the faith of the suffering.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 8:49–56 teach about Jesus’ power over death and faith's role in miracles?
options: Jesus has authority over death and requires faith for miracles to occur
Faith is irrelevant to miracles, which happen randomly
Miracles require human effort more than faith
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus has authority over death and requires faith for miracles to occur
questions.explanation: Luke 8:50 records Jesus' command to 'believe only,' and verses 52–55 demonstrate His power to raise the girl from death, combining the doctrines of divine authority over death and the necessity of faith.

questions.question: How does Luke 8:16–17 contribute to the narrative arc of revelation and judgment in Scripture?
options: It teaches that hidden things will be revealed, affirming divine judgment and revelation themes
It suggests that light should be hidden from the world
It emphasizes human secrecy over divine revelation
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that hidden things will be revealed, affirming divine judgment and revelation themes
questions.explanation: Luke 8:16–17 explains that nothing hidden will remain secret, linking to biblical themes of final revelation and judgment.
